==English== {{wp}} ===Alternative forms=== * {{alt|en|capitall||obsolete}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ˈkæpɪtəl/|[ˈkʰæpɪtʰəl]|~|[ˈkʰæpɪtʰl̩]|a=RP}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈkapɪtəl/|[ˈkʰapɪtʰəl]|~|[ˈkʰapɪtʰl̩]|a=SSB,Northern England,Scotland,Wales}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈkæpɪtəl/|[ˈkʰæpɪɾəl]|~|[ˈkʰæpɪɾl̩]|a=US,CA}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-capital.ogg|a=US}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈkæpətəl/|[ˈkʰæpəɾəl]|~|[ˈkʰæpəɾl̩]|a=AU}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈkɛpətəl/|[ˈkʰɛpəɾəl]|~|[ˈkʰɛpəɾl̩]|a=NZ}} * {{rhymes|en|æpɪtəl|s=3}} * {{hyph|en|cap|it|al}} * {{hmp|en|capitol}} ===Etymology 1=== {{ety|en|:inh|enm:capital>>>}} From {{inh|en|enm|capital}}, borrowed partly from {{der|en|fro|capital}} and partly from {{der|en|la|capitālis|t=of the head}}{{R:MED Online|entry=capitā̆l|pos=adj|id=MED6727}}{{R:OED Online|pos=''adj.'' and ''n.''2|noformat=1|id=8654406974}} (in sense “head of [[cattle]]”), from {{m|la|caput|t=head}} ({{cog|en|cap}}) + {{m|la|-ālis|pos=suffix forming adjectives}}. Use in trade and finance originated in Medieval economies when a common but expensive transaction involved trading heads of cattle. The noun is from the adjective.{{R:MED Online|entry=capitā̆l|pos=''n.''(1)|noformat=1|id=MED6725}} In the fourth sense, displaced native {{noncog|ang|hēafodburg}}, equivalent to {{l|en|head}} + {{l|en|borough|t=city}}. Compare {{m|en|chattel}} and {{m|en|kith and kine|t=all one’s possessions}}, which also use “cow” to mean “property”. {{doublet|en|cattle|chattel}}. ====Noun==== {{en-noun|~}} # {{senseid|en|Q8137}} {{lb|en|uncountable|business|finance|insurance|economics}} [[money|Money]] and [[wealth]]: the means to acquire or produce [[goods]] and [[services]], especially in a non-[[barter]] system. #: {{hypo|en|venture capital|risk capital}} #: {{nearsyn|en|asset}} #: {{ux|en|He does not have enough '''capital''' to start a business.}} # {{lb|en|uncountable|economics}} Already-produced durable goods available for use as a [[factor of production]], such as [[tool]]s and [[bulldozer]]s (equipment) and office buildings (structures). #: {{nearsyn|en|asset}} #: {{ux|en|He pointed out that it takes both labour and '''capital''' to produce goods.}} # {{lb|en|uncountable|politics}} The [[capitalist]] [[class]]; capital owners considered [[collectively]] as a [[politically]] [[influential]] group — commonly represented by [[wealthy]] individuals and [[private]] [[institutional investors]]. #: {{ux|en|The markets crashing symbolized '''capital'''’s discontent with the tax reforms passed.}} #: {{ux|en|He warned us darkly that '''capital''' will never be sated.}} # {{lb|en|countable}} A [[city]] [[designate]]d as a legislative seat by the [[government]] or some other [[authority]], often the city in which the government is [[locate]]d; otherwise the most [[important]] city within a [[country]] or a [[subdivision]] of it. #: {{ux|en|Washington D.C. is the '''capital''' of the United States of America.}} #: {{ux|en|The Welsh government claims that Cardiff is Europe’s youngest '''capital'''.}} #* {{quote-book |en |year=1995 |author=Linda Fang |title=The Chʻi-lin Purse: A Collection of Ancient Chinese Stories |url=https://archive.org/details/chilinpursecolle0000fang/ |location=[[New York]] |publisher=w:Farrar Straus Giroux |ISBN=0-374-31241-9 |LCCN=94-9909 |OCLC=214972990 |OL=1086004M |page=54 |pageurl=https://archive.org/details/chilinpursecolle0000fang/page/54/ |text=Lin Hsiang-ju immediately said to the king of Ch’in, “If ''Ta-wang'' wants fifteen cities from Chao, the king of Chao should also get something in return. What about giving him Hsien-yang as a gift?’ Hsien-yang was the '''capital''' of Ch’in.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-06-08|volume=407|issue=8839|page=52|magazine=w:The Economist |titleurl=http://www.economist.com/news/international/21579039-chinas-growing-empire-ports-abroad-mainly-about-trade-not-aggression-new-masters|title=The new masters and commanders |passage=From the ground, Colombo’s port does not look like much.{{...}}  But viewed from high up in one of the growing number of skyscrapers in Sri Lanka’s '''capital''', it is clear that something extraordinary is happening: China is creating a shipping hub just 200 miles from India’s southern tip.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20200929114134/https://www.economist.com/international/2013/06/08/the-new-masters-and-commanders}} #* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Edward-Isaac Dovere|title=Why these Democrats think 25 state legislative races are the key to securing the 2024 presidential election|url=https://www.cnn.com/2022/04/05/politics/democrats-state-legislative-races-20-million-investment|date=2022-04-05|passage=State legislative races tend to come cheap, with low turnout and tiny margins despite how state '''capitals''' have taken on an ever larger role amid legislative stalemate in Washington, DC. In 2020, a combined total of 46,000 votes determined which party was in majority control in 13 different state legislature chambers across the country.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20230111055638/https://www.cnn.com/2022/04/05/politics/democrats-state-legislative-races-20-million-investment|archivedate=11 January 2023}} #* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Richard Collett|title=He ran out of countries to visit, so he created his own|url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/06/08/travel/slowjamastan-micronation|date=2023-06-08|passage=Wearing his best suit and sunglasses, the sultan of Slowjamastan officially declared independence from the United States of America at 12:26 p.m. on December 1, 2021 as he broadcast the secession live from his open-air government “office” in Dublândia, the '''capital''' of the Republic of Slowjamastan.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260516010746/https://www.cnn.com/2023/06/08/travel/slowjamastan-micronation|archivedate=16 May 2026}} # {{lb|en|countable}} The most [[important]] [[city]] in the [[field]] specified. # {{lb|en|countable}} An [[uppercase]] [[letter]]. #: {{syn|en|caps|majuscule}} #: {{ant|en|minuscule}} # {{lb|en|uncountable}} [[knowledge|Knowledge]]; [[awareness]]; [[proficiency]]. #: {{ux|en|Interpreters need a good amount of cultural '''capital''' in order to function efficiently in the profession.}} # And I shall soon get a bonus."}} ===Etymology 2=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*kap-|id1=head}} {{multiple images |perrow=2 |total_width=320 |image1=Chapiteau-Parthenon.jpg |width1=1200|height1=803 |caption1=A [[Doric]] capital |image2=15 Halytska Square, Lviv (05).jpg |width2=3842|height2=2868 |caption2=An [[Ionic]] capital |image3=126 rue de rivoli Paris 2012 17.jpg |width3=5184|height3=3456 |caption3=A [[Corinthian]] capital |image4=Composite capital, Palace of Justice (today Ethnographic Museum), Budapest.jpg |width4=940|height4=1410 |caption4=A [[composite|Composite]] capital }} From {{inh|en|enm|capitale}}, partly from {{der|en|fro|capital}} and partly from {{der|en|la-lat|capitellum|t=capital or chapiter of a column}},{{R:OED Online|pos=''n.''1|noformat=1|id=2289960437}} a form of {{der|en|la|capitulum|t=head-like object or structure; chapter}} (whence English {{m|en|capitulum}}, {{m|en|chapter}}, and the synonym {{m|en|chapiter|t=uppermost part of a column}}), from {{m|la|caput|t=head}} + {{m|la|-ulum|pos=diminutive suffix}}. {{doublet|en|caddie|cadel|cadet|capitellum|caudillo}}. ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # {{senseid|en|architecture}} {{lb|en|countable|architectural element}} The uppermost part of a [[column]]. #: {{syn|en|chapiter}} #* {{RQ:Eddison Worm|page=3|passage=But a great wonder of this chamber, and a marvel to behold, was how the '''capital''' of every one of the four-and-twenty pillars was hewn from a single precious stone, carved by the hand of some sculptor of long ago into the living form of a monster: {{...}}}} =====Translations===== {{trans-top|uppermost part of a column|id=architecture}} * Arabic: * Armenian: * Azerbaijani: * Basque: * Belarusian: * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Chinese: * Czech: * Danish: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Estonian: * Finnish: * French: * Galician: * Georgian: * German: * Greek: * Hebrew: * Hungarian: * Icelandic: * Ido: * Indonesian: * Italian: * Japanese: * Korean: * Latvian: * Lithuanian: * Macedonian: * Norwegian: * Occitan: * Persian: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Romanian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|капите́ль|f}} * Serbo-Croatian: * Slovak: * Slovene: * Spanish: * Swedish: * Turkish: * Ukrainian: * Uzbek: {{trans-bottom}} ===References=== * {{R:Online Etymology Dictionary}} * {{R:OneLook}} {{reflist}} ===Anagrams=== * {{anagrams|en|a=aacilpt|palatic|placita}} {{C|en|Capitalism}}
